Getting started with metacleaner

Source: vignettes/metacleaner.Rmd
metacleaner.Rmd

What metacleaner does

Reference databases for DNA metabarcoding (for example plant ITS2 databases built from NCBI GenBank) contain sequences with the wrong name: fungal sequences submitted as plants, sequences labeled with the wrong genus, and sequences that are identical in several genera and so cannot identify any of them. Reads that match these entries are assigned to the wrong taxon.

metacleaner checks every sequence in your database (the query) in three steps:

  1. Does it match a sequence in a database of things that should not be there (the contaminants, e.g. fungal ITS)? Then it is removed.
  2. Does it match a sequence in a database of things that should be there (the reference, e.g. all plant ITS)? If not, it is removed.
  3. Do the reference sequences it matches have the same taxonomy as the query at the level you choose (genus by default)? If they belong to a different genus, or to several genera, it is removed.

A “match” means at least identity percent identical over at least coverage percent of the query’s length. Both are 100 by default, so only identical sequences count.

You need no programming experience and no other software: everything, including the sequence search, is built into the package.

Installing 

install.packages("metacleaner", dependencies = TRUE)

dependencies = TRUE also installs the optional packages used to download data and taxonomy from NCBI.

Your files

You need:

  • query: the FASTA file you want to clean. Each header must start with an NCBI accession, e.g. >MW545606.1 (anything after the first space is ignored). Sequences may be on one line or wrapped over several lines.
  • reference: a FASTA file of sequences from the group you want to keep.
  • contaminants (optional but recommended): a FASTA file of sequences from groups you want to remove.
  • taxonomy: where to find the taxonomy of each accession. This can be a taxonomy file (for example the .tax file made with MetaCurator or taxonomizr), or simply "ncbi" to look it up online.

build_reference_db() can create the reference and contaminant files for you; see vignette("building-databases").

A worked example

metacleaner includes a small real example: plant ITS2 sequences from NCBI (the query), a plant reference set, a fungal contaminant set and a taxonomy file. system.file() just finds these example files on your computer; for your own data, put your file paths in quotes instead, e.g. query = "C:/data/ITS2_database.fasta".

library(metacleaner)
ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "metacleaner")

result <- clean_reference(
  query        = ex("query.fasta"),
  reference    = ex("reference.fasta"),
  contaminants = ex("contaminants.fasta"),
  taxonomy     = ex("taxonomy.tax"),
  level        = "genus"
)
#> metacleaner: reading sequences
#>   52 query, 168 reference, 33 contaminant sequences
#> Step 1/3: searching the contaminant database
#> Step 2/3: searching the reference database
#> Step 3/3: comparing taxonomy at genus level
#>   3 sequence(s) match the contaminant database
#>   retrieving taxonomy for 171 sequence(s)
#>   0 sequence(s) have no qualifying match in the reference database (0 more rescued by their best hit)
#>   6 sequence(s) match more than one genus; 0 match a different genus
#> Done: kept 40 of 52 sequences, flagged 12 (0.3 s).
result
#> <metacleaner result>
#>   query sequences:   52
#>   kept:              40
#>   flagged:           12
#>     matches multiple genus                   6
#>     matches contaminant database             3
#>     no taxonomy for query at genus           3
#>   settings: identity >= 100%, coverage >= 100%, level = genus, engine = native
#> Use write_results() to save the cleaned database and report.

The flagged sequences, with the reason and the hit that caused it:

head(result$flagged[, c("id", "reason", "top_hit", "hit_taxa")])
#>           id                         reason    top_hit              hit_taxa
#> 1 KF984840.1   matches contaminant database KF984840.1                  <NA>
#> 2 MN228964.1 no taxonomy for query at genus MN228964.1             <unknown>
#> 3 MW545606.1         matches multiple genus MW545600.1 Chrysanthemum; Ajania
#> 4 MW545611.1         matches multiple genus MW545600.1 Chrysanthemum; Ajania
#> 5 MW545649.1         matches multiple genus MW545607.1 Ajania; Chrysanthemum
#> 6 MW545773.1         matches multiple genus MW545787.1 Artemisia; Filifolium

Save the cleaned database and the report:

write_results(result, outdir = "cleaned", prefix = "ITS2")

This writes four files into the folder cleaned:

File Contents
ITS2_clean.fasta the sequences that were kept
ITS2_clean.tax their taxonomy (same format as the old metacleaner / MetaCurator input)
ITS2_flagged.tsv every removed sequence, its taxonomy, the hit that caused the removal, that hit’s taxonomy and the reason; open it in Excel
ITS2_summary.txt the settings used and the number removed for each reason

You can also do it all in one go by giving outdir to clean_reference().

Choosing settings

  • identity and coverage (default 100 and 100). Lowering them, e.g. to identity = 99, coverage = 95, also counts near-identical matches, so more sequences are checked against more relatives. The search is slower and stricter.
  • level (default "genus"). The rank at which the query and its matches must agree. Use "family" for a more lenient clean or "species" for a stricter one.
  • require, e.g. require = c(class = "Magnoliopsida"), removes any sequence that matches something outside flowering plants.
  • rescue (default TRUE). A sequence without a full-length identical match is kept if its closest match is in the same genus. Set rescue = FALSE to remove all such sequences.
  • threads. Use more CPU cores for large databases, e.g. threads = 8, or threads = "auto" to use all but one.

The reasons a sequence is removed

Reason Meaning
matches contaminant database identical (at your thresholds) to a sequence in the contaminant database
no match in reference database not found in the reference database
hit outside required … matches something outside the taxon given in require
no taxonomy for query at … the sequence’s own taxonomy is unknown at level
matches multiple … it matches reference sequences from more than one genus (or other level)
matches different … all its matches belong to one other genus

The checks run in this order and each sequence gets the first reason that applies; see ?classify_queries for details.

Coming from the command-line version

metacleaner.py option R argument
-q/--query query
-x/-f (badblastdb) contaminants (a FASTA file; no BLAST database needed)
-y/-g (goodblastdb) reference
-d/--taxadb taxonomy = "path/to/accessionTaxa.sql"
-e/--pident identity
-v/--qcovs coverage
-l/--filterlevel level
-w/--addfilter class,Magnoliopsida require = c(class = "Magnoliopsida")
-t/--threads threads
-o/--outdir outdir
-c/--chunks, -s/--sortonly not needed

To reproduce the BLAST-based search of the old version exactly, install BLAST+ and use engine = "blast".
